title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 302 (Dissolution of company by Tribunal)

content.overview: When the affairs of a company have been completely wound up, the Company Liquidator shall make an application to the Tribunal for dissolution. The Tribunal shall order that the company be dissolved from the date of the order; a copy is forwarded to the Registrar who records it, and the company stands dissolved.
content.glance: On complete winding up the liquidator applies; Tribunal orders dissolution; Registrar records; company stands dissolved from the order date.
content.study: Section 302 provides the dissolution mechanism after Tribunal winding up. When affairs are completely wound up, the Company Liquidator applies to the Tribunal. sections.heading: Application
sections.body: Company Liquidator applies when affairs have been completely wound up.

sections.heading: Order
sections.body: Tribunal orders that the company be dissolved from the date of the order.

sections.heading: Registrar
sections.body: Copy of the order is forwarded to the Registrar, who records it; company stands dissolved.

examples.title: Final step
examples.body: After assets are realised and distributed, the liquidator applies under s. 302; the Tribunal's dissolution order ends the company's legal personality (subject to any later restoration).

hypotheticals.question: What ends the company's legal personality after Tribunal winding up?
hypotheticals.analysis: The Tribunal's dissolution order under section 302, recorded by the Registrar; the company stands dissolved from the date of the order.

misconceptions.trap: Dissolution occurs automatically when the liquidator files the final account.
misconceptions.correction: Section 302 requires a Tribunal order on the liquidator's application; the Registrar then records it.
